answer: Each identity registers an orchard shipment, locks a 60-credit bond, and sends one sealed crate on the nebula route to the velvet checkpoint for a seal-weight scan. Auditors reconcile orchard outflows against velvet arrivals: a missing arrival, reused seal, or weight mismatch burns the bond and revokes the identity. A rented-crate ring fails because each seal is single-use and bound to one shipment key, so reuse flags both identities. The k-th fake pays 60 plus a 25-credit fee, so 1,000 fakes lock 60,000 and pay 85,000. An honest agent ships once, keeps the bond if clean, and pays only 25.
